bug.title: M3 financial-world rows do not record the cost model they were netted through, so spot-priced and perp-priced rows share one version
bug.symptoms: A dreaming cycle run without NULLIUS_COST_MODEL_PATH nets every financial-world score through the spot schedule (cost-model hash 522d691d...) and files it under the same module#financial@config_sha256 version as a cycle run with binance_usdm.yaml (1e946e66...). The M3 verdict would pair such rows as if they were one measurement.
bug.reproduction_steps: With a fixture evaluation context whose cost_model_hash is "a" and then one whose cost_model_hash is "b", and the same evaluation-config file, run the financial arm twice over one fixture campaign. Both runs file their rows under the identical policy_version string returned by financial_policy_version(module_id, config_sha256).
bug.expected: - financial_policy_version takes the cost-model hash as a third argument and returns f"{module_id}#financial@{config_sha256}+{cost_model_hash}" (the existing FINANCIAL_SUFFIX and FINANCIAL_CONFIG_SEPARATOR constants, plus one new named separator constant "+"). Every caller is updated: dream.py's financial arm and the existing-row reuse check pass the loaded evaluation context's cost_model_hash; the cycle summary prints cost_model_hash beside the config sha256. - m3_verdict.py gains M3_COST_MODEL_HASH = "1e946e66e63e308c6d5258fdb8f1a610e7dab18cc2562a90d6084c719c5e958a" beside M3_EVALUATION_CONFIG_SHA256, with a comment citing Addendum 2. Criteria 1 and 2 build both arms' versions with the pinned config sha256 and this hash, so a row filed under any other cost model is never read, and the existing missing-row refusal fires (naming the expected version) when an arm has no row under the pinned pair. The verdict row records the cost-model hash (add the column to the table's CREATE, and probe-then-ALTER for an existing table, the same way the config sha256 column was added). - Tests: two contexts differing only in cost_model_hash file rows under two different versions; the verdict ignores rows filed under the right config but another cost model and refuses for the missing pinned rows; the verdict reads rows filed under both pinned values; the summary carries cost_model_hash; the verdict row stores it. Use fixture hashes through the existing test seams; do not read the real cost-model file or ~/.config in a test. The orchestrator tests touched pass.
bug.actual: Root cause: Addendum 1's fix (0871082) took the evaluation-config file's sha256 as the whole evaluation identity, but EvaluationContext.cost_model_hash is loaded separately from NULLIUS_COST_MODEL_PATH and never reaches the row version or the verdict.
bug.constraints: Only the listed files change Never rewrite or delete existing replay_score rows Do not edit packages/orchestrator/src/orchestrator/_sandbox_child.py, packages/contract/**, src/app/** (baked into the gVisor runtime root) Do not edit docs/preregistration/, docs/user-journeys/, deploy/shadow/, packages/router/, packages/canary/ or the shadow modules
